bc_cosmic_boulder.blurb: Cosmic Boulder is one of the sectors of the Pemberton boulder field in the forest north of Whistler, in the Sea to Sky corridor. It holds eleven problems and nothing else, so this is a bouldering stop rather than a roped crag. Difficulty runs from V2 up to V8, but the bulk sits in the V3 to V5 range, which makes it a good fit for a mid-grade session, with a couple of harder lines for the strong. The block stands near the end of the trail and is easy to spot beside the path. Landings around the field are generally friendly, and a single pad is usually enough.

bc_a_campground_boulders.blurb: Campground Boulders is the southernmost zone of the Grand Wall Boulders at the foot of the Stawamus Chief near Squamish. The blocks sit in forest right beside the provincial park campground, with most problems lying between the tent sites and the cliff above. Eleven problems are recorded, all bouldering, spread from VB-level warm-ups through the middle grades to a handful of hard lines in the V6 to V7 range and one much harder test around V10. Like the wider Grand Wall area, the setting is shady and cool, so it suits warm days, and the landings are likely to be rooty, so bring pads.

bc_smallville.blurb: Smallville is a compact boulder in the Hunter Creek bouldering area of the Fraser Valley, filed under the Sleight of Hand sector. Eleven problems wrap around the block, from easy traverses and a V1 up through a solid middle band at V4 and V5, with the hardest line around V6. It is a quiet, low-elevation spot among evergreens with the river audible nearby, and the rock is friction-oriented, so skin and footwork matter. Late morning into early afternoon brings the sun. Follow the woodland path linking Sleight of Hand and the Ice Box boulder and look left to find it. Bring a standard pad.

bc_the_chamber.blurb: The Chamber is a cave-like feature in the Lower Right section of the Stacks, a cluster of boulders below a wall near Hope in the Fraser Valley. One large block leans onto a slightly smaller one, and the east side overhangs at roughly thirty degrees, an uncommon feature for the region. The face is highly featured and carries a handful of lines. The eleven problems here are all hard: nothing easier than V4, with most of them sitting between V7 and V9, so this is a spot for strong boulderers. Approach is short, under five minutes from the car on a path through trees, then skirt the talus to the cave.

bc_starr_wall.blurb: Starr Wall is the main trad cliff of the Malamute, across the road from the Stawamus Chief parking in Squamish. Ten of its eleven routes are trad, with a single sport line, and the grades run from the easy 5.7 and 5.8 range to a couple of 5.11s and one 5.12, with the 5.10 band holding about half of everything. The cliff catches wind and stays shaded into the early afternoon, which can feel chilly outside summer. The walk in follows the main trail to the top of the Malamute, and the wall is about a hundred metres further on, to climbers' right.
